Summary: The sources define F1 as the harmonic mean of precision and recall over the tokens shared between the predicted answer and the gold answer, used to evaluate short free-form QA. The joint F1 combines the performance of both the answer span and the supporting facts, calculated as P^(joint) = P^(ans)P^(sup), R^(joint) = R^(ans)R^(sup), and Joint F1 = 2P^(joint)R^(joint)/(P^(joint) + R^(joint)). Baseline BiDAF++ models achieve 59% F1 on the answer in the distractor setting, with joint F1 around 41%. The dataset HotpotQA, introduced by Yang et al. in 2018, requires multi-hop reasoning over multiple supporting documents and uses EM and F1 for both answers and supporting facts.
